compare.title: Why most language apps get abandoned – and this one doesn't
compare.subtitle: The problem was never your discipline. It was the format.

old.title: You memorize words you can't actually use
old.text: Lists and flashcards with no context. Gone again by tomorrow.

new.title: Words turn up inside real sentences
new.text: You see how a word behaves in context, so it sticks without being forced.

old.title: The same exercises every single day
old.text: It gets dull, motivation drops, and the app sits unopened after week one.

new.title: You read what you'd read anyway
new.text: Bestsellers, strange true stories, popular science – material you come back to on your own.

old.title: Reading the original is too hard
old.text: Unknown words everywhere, the plot slips away, you quit on page one.

new.title: Parallel translation, plus adaptation
new.text: The translation sits right beside the text, and a book that's too hard can be rewritten at your level.

old.title: You read whatever the catalog happens to have
old.text: A fixed library. No way to bring your own book.

new.title: Any book or text becomes your textbook
new.text: Hand the app the books you love and the documents you need, and it gives them back with parallel translation, audio and word review.

old.title: You read and listen, but it's all passive
old.text: Nowhere to speak or write, so the skill never sets.

new.title: You don't only read – you speak and write
new.text: You talk over the book you just finished with AI, so there's no topic to invent. When you have something to say, saying and writing it gets easy.

method.title: All 7 language skills in one place
method.subtitle: Knowing a language is seven skills. Lingo7 trains them together instead of one at a time, so each one pulls the others along.

skills.title: Reading
skills.text: Read the original or an adapted version with the translation right beside it – fast, and without a dictionary.

skills.title: Listening
skills.text: Audiobooks and a listen-while-you-read mode – one of the most effective ways to train your ear.

skills.title: Vocabulary
skills.text: New words stick as you read, without drilling them. Exercises and spaced repetition lock them in for the long run.

skills.title: Grammar
skills.text: The best way to absorb grammar is to watch the rules do their work inside a real sentence.

skills.title: Writing
skills.text: AI chat: you discuss what you just read, so there's always something to write about. It helps you shape the thought and catches your mistakes.

skills.title: Speaking
skills.text: Shadowing: you repeat after the narrator out loud and build fluency, rhythm and intonation.

skills.title: Pronunciation
skills.text: Pronunciation exercises help you move your accent closer to the way a native speaker sounds.

conductor.title: The app will tell you what to do today
conductor.text: It picks the right activity at the right moment – read, repeat out loud, lock in words or talk a chapter over with AI. You never have to decide where to start or what comes next.
conductor.caption: A sample session for today – the app will build yours.

steps.title: How to learn a language from books: five steps
steps.subtitle: No elaborate method. One clear cycle, with content good enough to carry you through it.

items.title: Pick your content
items.text: Bestseller summaries, classics, short stories – by mood, by level, by the time you have.

items.title: Read with parallel translation
items.text: Original and translation side by side; tap a word for its meaning, its audio, or to save it.

items.title: Learn the words
items.text: Saved words come back in exercises that work different kinds of memory, spaced out over time.

items.title: Listen and repeat out loud
items.text: Every sentence has audio: listen, then shadow the narrator – that's where pronunciation and intonation come from.

items.title: Talk the book over with AI
items.text: The AI goes through the book with you – you practice writing and speaking, and learn to put thoughts into a new language.

library.title: {target} books with translation – by level, A1 to C1
library.subtitle: You're not only learning a language, you're learning something. Material for every level, from first steps to advanced.

panels.title: Read the great books in the original – with a safety net
panels.text: Adapted and original versions for different levels, from The Little Prince to Hawking. Parallel translation keeps even difficult prose readable.

panels.title: The gist of the world's best books in 7–15 minutes
panels.text: The key ideas of global bestsellers, retold short – in the language you're learning. Grow and learn the language in the same sitting.

panels.title: 5 minutes a day: one good fact and a few new words
panels.text: Space, psychology, business, nature, technology – hundreds of short articles on any subject. Learn something new every day, and the language comes with it.

examples: Think and Grow Rich • The 80/20 Principle • The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People • The Power of Now

cards.title: Bestsellers in the original

cards.title: The language your work and studies need

pains.title: What gets in the way – and what Lingo7 does about it
pains.subtitle: It isn't a question of ability. It's a question of format.

answers.title: “I'm embarrassed to speak and get it wrong”
answers.text: Shadowing means repeating phrases after the narrator out loud, on your own, with nobody grading you. That's where pronunciation comes from. In the AI chat you work on phrasing in writing, and it corrects you gently.

answers.title: “I get bored fast”
answers.text: Instead of interchangeable lessons: books, bestsellers and articles on subjects you'd read about anyway. When the content pulls, coming back is easy.

answers.title: “I see the words but they don't stay”
answers.text: One tap saves a word out of its sentence, then it comes back as a card on a spaced schedule. Remembering stops being a matter of luck.

answers.title: “Reading the original is too hard for me”
answers.text: Parallel translation with the sentences lined up – no jumping into a translator every other line.

answers.title: “I can't follow the spoken language”
answers.text: Listen-and-read mode ties the sound of a word to its spelling and its meaning. Your ear gets used to the language naturally.

answers.title: “I don't have the time”
answers.text: Short formats and quick sessions – even 5-10 minutes a day keeps you in the rhythm.

answers.title: “I need a rare language”
answers.text: 49 languages, rare ones included. And you learn any of them from your own native language.

answers.title: “I'm afraid it won't suit me”
answers.text: If you can read, it suits you. No prior knowledge, grammar or preparation required – start with any book at your level.

languages.title: 49 languages, from the common to the rare
languages.subtitle: Learn any language from your own native one – not only through English, the way most apps make you.
languages.pairs: 49 × 48 = 2352 language pairs. Pick any combination: the language you're learning, and the language you read the translation in.

items.q: Will Lingo7 work for a complete beginner?
items.a: Yes. There's material at every level, and parallel translation makes the text understandable from the very start.

items.q: What level do I need to read in the original?
items.a: Any level. The parallel translation removes the need for a dictionary, and a book that is too hard can be rewritten simpler – the same story and characters, but the grammar and words of your level. Everything is marked A1 to C1.

items.q: Can I study 10 minutes a day?
items.a: Yes. Short articles, book summaries and word cards are made for short daily sessions.
49 languages, and you can learn any of them from your own native language – not only through English. That's 49 × 48 = 2352 language pairs, rare languages included.

items.q: How is this different from the usual language apps?
items.a: Instead of disconnected exercises, you learn from content that interests you, with every skill tied into one loop: you read and listen, save words for spaced review, pick up grammar in context, work on speech through shadowing and on writing in the AI chat. And you can upload your own book or document.

Yes. For speech there's shadowing – you repeat phrases after the narrator out loud and build pronunciation and intonation. For writing there's the AI chat: you discuss what you've read, and it helps you phrase things and finds your mistakes. Live conversation with a person isn't there yet – it's planned.

items.q: Which file formats can I upload?
items.a: PDF, EPUB, FB2 and TXT. Upload work documents, favorite books or articles – the app builds the parallel translation, adds audio and collects the new words into the trainer.
